title: Legal Manager
description:
**Overview**
 CACTUS is a remote\-first organization and we embrace an accelerate from anywhere culture. You may be required to travel to our Mumbai office based on business requirements or for company/team events.
   

 We are a dynamic \& centralized team of talented Legal professionals. The Manager, Legal, will be part of this centralized team, assisting in legal operations for CACTUS and its overseas entities. One of the most exciting parts of this role is the opportunity to work on diverse assignments and exposure to various legal and compliance matters on a global scale making it a unique opportunity for dynamic legal professionals.
   

**Responsibilities**
* Contract Management: Draft, review, negotiate, and finalize business contracts (MSAs, vendor agreements, NDAs, lease deeds, etc.) and optimize contract processes using technology.
* Legal Advisory \& Risk Management: Provide actionable legal advice, identify risks, and develop mitigation strategies for business initiatives.
* Project Management: Independently manage legal workstreams and projects, co\-ordinate with cross\-functional stakeholders, and drive matters to timely closure.
* Compliance \& Policy: Develop and monitor corporate policies, ensure regulatory compliance across jurisdictions, and stay updated on legislative changes.
* Data Privacy: Advice on compliance with global data protection laws (e.g., GDPR, DPDPA) and standardize data handling practices.
* Intellectual Property: Manage IP protection, enforcement, and filings; draft IP\-related clauses and notices.
* Litigation: Handle legal notices, pre\-litigation matters, and coordinate with external counsel for litigation.
* Employment \& Labor Laws: Experience in employment and labour law, with the ability to advise on employment\-related matters and support HR and business stakeholders on practical legal and compliance requirements.
* Operational Excellence: Drive process improvement, standardization, and automation across legal operations, including developing SOPs, templates, workflows, trackers, and other tools to improve efficiency and consistency.


**Qualifications And Prerequisites**
* Bachelor of Law (LLB) with work experience of 8\-10 years.
* Business Partnering, working closely with internal teams to address legal concerns and provide practical solutions that align with business objectives.
* Strong communication skills to simplify legal concepts for non\-legal teams.
* Ability to independently manage projects, priorities, stakeholders, and high volumes in a fast\-paced environment.
* Strong organizational and multi\-tasking skills with attention to detail.
* Fast closure and efficiency.
* Exceptional drafting, negotiation, and analytical skills.
* Demonstrated expertise in international corporate and contractual laws.
* Strong interpersonal and stakeholder management capabilities.
* Highly motivated, independent, with a quality and results\-oriented mindset.


 Application Process
   

 Before applying, please ensure you meet the role requirements listed above and have legal authorization to work in the country where this role is advertised.Our selection process typically involves an initial screening by a recruiter, a technical assessment, and two to three interview rounds. For this role, there will be 2\-3 rounds of interview including an in\-person meeting (for Mumbai based candidates).
   

**Equal Opportunity**
 Our hiring practices reflect our commitment to providing equal opportunities and creating an environment where everyone can thrive, develop, and succeed. We celebrate the uniqueness of our team members and prohibit discrimination of any kind, based on race, color, religion, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, or any other protected characteristic.
   

**Accelerating from Anywhere**
 As a remote\-first organization, these are essential attributes we look for in all our candidates.
   

* Taking ownership of your work with minimal supervision, showing strong ability to organize, prioritize and deliver results independently.
* Documenting work that brings everyone on the same page.
* Maturity to choose between synchronous and asynchronous collaboration.
* Effectively collaborating with colleagues across different time zones by setting dedicated hours for collaboration and keeping team members updated through your MS Teams status.


**About CACTUS**
 Established in 2002, Cactus Communications (cactusglobal.com) is a leading technology company that specializes in expert services and AI\-driven products which improve how research gets funded, published, communicated, and discovered. Its flagship brand Editage offers a comprehensive suite of researcher solutions, including expert services and cutting\-edge AI products like Mind the Graph, Paperpal, and R Discovery. With offices in Princeton, London, Singapore, Beijing, Shanghai, Seoul, Tokyo, and Mumbai and a global workforce of over 3,000 experts, CACTUS is a pioneer in workplace best practices and has been consistently recognized as a great place to work.

title: Company Secretary
description:
**Role Overview** 




 To ensure compliance with the Companies Act, 2013 and other applicable corporate laws by managing secretarial activities, statutory compliances, Board processes, and corporate governance requirements for Essar Ports and its group entities. The role will support the Board, senior management, and business teams in maintaining high standards of governance and regulatory compliance.
 



**Key Responsibilities** 




**Corporate Secretarial \& Governance** 



* Ensure compliance with the Companies Act, 2013, Secretarial Standards, and other applicable statutory requirements.
* Assist in implementing corporate governance practices and ensuring adherence across the organization.
* Track regulatory changes and support implementation of new compliance requirements.



**Board \& Committee Management** 



* Coordinate Board, Committee, and Shareholders' Meetings.
* Prepare notices, agendas, Board papers, resolutions, and minutes.
* Maintain Board records and ensure timely closure of action items arising from meetings.



**Statutory Compliance** 



* Ensure timely filing of statutory forms, annual returns, and other regulatory submissions with the Registrar of Companies (ROC) and Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA).
* Maintain statutory registers, records, licenses, and corporate documents.
* Coordinate Secretarial Audit and ensure timely closure of observations.
* Support compliance with FEMA and RBI regulations, wherever applicable.



**Compliance Management** 



* Develop and maintain statutory compliance calendars and trackers.
* Coordinate with internal stakeholders to ensure timely completion of compliance requirements.
* Support internal and external audits related to secretarial and corporate governance matters.



**Corporate Transactions** 



* Support incorporation of companies, changes in capital structure, alteration of constitutional documents, and other corporate actions.
* Assist in mergers, acquisitions, restructuring, financing transactions, and due diligence from a secretarial perspective.
* Coordinate execution and maintenance of statutory approvals and documentation.



**Stakeholder Coordination** 



* Liaise with regulatory authorities, consultants, statutory auditors, secretarial auditors, banks, and legal advisors.
* Work closely with Finance, Legal, Taxation, and Business teams on corporate compliance matters.



**Documentation \& Record Management** 



* Maintain accurate statutory records and corporate documentation.
* Ensure safe custody and digitization of corporate records.
* Prepare periodic compliance reports and updates for senior management.



**Education** 



* Qualified Company Secretary (Member of ICSI) – Mandatory.
* LLB will be an added advantage.



**Experience** 



* **7\+ years of post\-qualification experience** 
 in corporate secretarial functions.
* Experience in infrastructure, ports, logistics, manufacturing, EPC, or large corporate organizations will be added advantage.
* Exposure to Board processes, statutory filings, and corporate governance practices is desirable.

description:

 The story of The Leela Palaces, Hotels and Resorts began when its founder Late Capt. CP Krishnan Nair opened The Leela Mumbai in 1986\. For over three decades, The Leela has been on a journey to delight guests by providing unparalleled luxury in captivating environs ensconced in the lap of nature, wrapped in the graciousness of Indian hospitality.
 



  





 Headquartered in Mumbai, The Leela Palaces, Hotels and Resorts is owned by a Brookfield Asset Management\- sponsored private real estate fund and operates thirteen award\-winning properties in major cities and leisure destinations across India. These include the flagship hotel in the capital city of New Delhi, Bengaluru, Chennai, Udaipur, Jaipur, Gurugram, East Delhi, Mumbai, Gandhinagar, Kovalam, and Ashtamudi. The brand is also delighted to announce the upcoming opening of its latest property in Hyderabad. The Leela has a strong pipeline of future projects. The brand celebrates each hotel through its unique location, art, culture, and cuisine with thoughtful services, celebratory rituals, and immersive experiences. The Leela Palaces, Hotels and Resorts was voted the World’s Best Hotel Brand twice in a row by Travel \+ Leisure, USA, World’s Best Awards Survey, 2020 2021, 2023,2024, 2026\. An epitome of true Indian luxury hospitality, The Leela is committed to providing guests with unforgettable stays in settings that capture the essence of India. The brand has a marketing alliance with US\- based Preferred Hotels \& Resorts and is a member of the Global Hotel Alliance.
 



  





 Why join The Leela?
 



  




* **Award\-Winning Brand** 
 : Join a brand that has been recognized as one of the World’sBest Hotel Brands for two consecutive years.
* **Commitment to Excellence** 
 : Be part of a team that is dedicated to providing the highest standards of service and hospitality.
* **Innovative Environment** 
 : Be part of a team that encourages creativity and innovation, ensuring that we stay at the forefront of luxury hospitality.
* **Career Growth** 
 : Benefit from our strong pipeline of future projects and opportunities for career advancement within The Leela and our global alliances.
* **Cultural Experiences** 
 : Engage with the rich cultural tapestry of India, bringing unique and authentic experiences to our discerning guests.



  





 Position Overview
 



**Reporting to: Vice President \- Procurement** 




**Location:** 
 The Leela Corporate Office, Mumbai
 



 The Manager / Senior Manager – Procurement \& Contracts (Civil) will be responsible for managing procurement and contracting activities related to civil and interior works across project developments. This role involves leading the procurement lifecycle for construction packages, evaluating technical and commercial requirements, managing contract finalization, and ensuring adherence to contractual, regulatory, and project requirements.
 



  





 The incumbent will work closely with project teams, consultants, contractors, and internal stakeholders to support the successful delivery of project procurement objectives. The role requires strong expertise in contract management, commercial negotiations, technical evaluation of civil and interior packages, and a thorough understanding of construction industry practices and standards.
 



  





**Responsibilities:** 




**Procurement \& Contract Finalization** 



* Lead procurement and contract finalization activities for moderate\-value civil and interior work packages.
* Manage sourcing, bid evaluation, commercial discussions, and award recommendations for project\-related procurement requirements.
* Review technical and commercial submissions to ensure alignment with project objectives and contractual requirements.
* Support the preparation, negotiation, execution, and administration of contracts.
* Ensure procurement activities are conducted in accordance with approved processes and governance requirements.



**Technical Evaluation \& Commercial Assessment** 



* Interpret and evaluate civil and interior drawings, specifications, and Bills of Quantities (BOQs).
* Assess contractor submissions from both technical and commercial perspectives.
* Validate scope requirements and ensure completeness during tendering and contracting stages.
* Assist project stakeholders in evaluating procurement options and contractor capabilities.
* Support cost optimization initiatives while maintaining quality and project standards.



**Contract Administration** 



* Monitor contractual obligations, terms, and performance throughout the contract lifecycle.
* Manage contract variations, non\-tendered (NT) items, and change management requirements.
* Support the resolution of contractual claims and disputes through effective documentation and stakeholder coordination.
* Ensure adherence to approved contract conditions and commercial commitments.
* Maintain contract records and support documentation for governance and audit requirements.



  





**Compliance \& Industry Standards** 



* Ensure procurement and contracting activities comply with applicable standards, regulations, and organizational requirements.
* Maintain awareness of safety protocols and regulatory requirements applicable to construction projects.
* Apply knowledge of NBC and BIS codes during procurement and contract evaluation activities.
* Ensure awareness and application of relevant contract laws and regulations.
* Support risk identification and mitigation throughout the procurement process.



**Market Intelligence \& Industry Awareness** 



* Stay informed about industry trends, market conditions, and technological developments related to civil and interior materials.
* Monitor market developments to support informed procurement decisions.
* Identify opportunities to improve procurement effectiveness through industry best practices and innovation.
* Provide market insights and recommendations that support project procurement requirements.

**Job Description**
 About Artha Group:
   

  

 Artha Group is a distinguished player in the global investment landscape, managing over ₹2,300 crores in assets under management (AUM). Our diverse portfolio spans 130\+ startups, with 32\+ successful exits, and 10\+ renewable energy projects. As both a General Partner (GP) and a Limited Partner (LP) in various micro\-VC funds, we operate a unique self\-sustaining investment model that reinvests returns from high\-yielding renewable energy assets into high\-potential startups. With a focus on sectors such as B2B SaaS, FinTech, and space tech, we are actively expanding our global footprint, leveraging offshore structures to explore new opportunities worldwide.
   

  

**Role Overview**
 Artha Group is seeking a highly detail\-oriented and experienced Associate \- Compliance to ensure compliance with all regulatory frameworks pertaining to our SEBI\-registered Alternative Investment Fund (AIF). The ideal candidate will be responsible for managing and overseeing compliance procedures related to both investments made and investments taken by the fund. The role requires a strong understanding of compliance requirements specific to venture capital funds, including SEBI regulations, fund documentation, and financial disclosures.
   

  

 This individual will maintain a detailed compliance calendar, ensuring the timely submission of all necessary filings and reports, and collaborate with internal teams to ensure alignment with legal and regulatory requirements. A Company Secretary (CS) certification is mandatory for this role.
   

  

**Key Responsibilities**
* Compliance Management for Venture Capital Fund:


 Ensure full compliance with SEBI (Securities and Exchange Board of India) regulations governing the operations of an AIF (Alternative Investment Fund), including investment compliance.Maintain and update compliance procedures for all investment activities—both incoming (capital raised) and outgoing (investments made).Review, manage, and maintain statutory documentation related to the fund, ensuring all records are accurate and up to date.
   

  

* Compliance Calendar and Regulatory Filings:


 Develop and manage a comprehensive compliance calendar that tracks all regulatory filing deadlines (annual, quarterly, monthly, and weekly).Prepare and submit all mandatory reports, including those related to fund performance, investor communication, financial reporting, and compliance disclosures.Ensure timely filing of statutory forms, SEBI filings, and other regulatory submissions as required by law.
   

  

* Internal Coordination and Audit Support:


 Collaborate with internal teams, including legal, finance, and operations, to ensure all processes align with regulatory requirements.Assist in preparing for internal and external audits by providing all necessary documentation and supporting materials.Conduct periodic internal reviews to ensure all compliance policies are properly implemented and followed by all teams.
   

  

* Compliance Reporting and Documentation:


 Provide regular updates to senior management on compliance activities and report any potential compliance risks or issues.Maintain comprehensive records of all compliance activities, including regulatory filings, approvals, and other essential documents.Ensure that all compliance policies are documented, communicated, and adhered to within the organization.
   

  

* Risk Management:


 Identify potential regulatory or compliance risks associated with investments, transactions, and fund operations, and suggest appropriate mitigating actions.Proactively monitor changes in SEBI and other regulatory frameworks that may impact the venture capital fund, and ensure timely adaptation to new regulations.
   

  

**Requirements**
 Must be a Company Secretary (CS) with experience in managing compliance for a venture capital fund or financial institution.3\-5 years of experience in compliance management, preferably within the venture capital, private equity, or investment management sectors.Strong understanding of SEBI regulations and compliance frameworks applicable to AIFs (Alternative Investment Funds).Demonstrated ability to manage and maintain a compliance calendar, ensuring the timely filing of all regulatory reports and disclosures.Excellent organizational and communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively across teams.Proficiency in compliance software and familiarity with the legal aspects of fund management.

 Total annual salary \- ₹21,00,000Fixed annual salary \- ₹18,00,000Retention bonus \- ₹3,00,000

title: Assistant Vice President - Legal Discovery Management
description:
**Job Description**
**Job Title**
 eDiscovery Operations – Sr Counsel
   

  

**Description**
 Legal Discovery Management (LDM) is an internal organization within the firm's Litigation Department.
   

  

 As a Senior Counsel in Legal discovery operations team you will support and facilitate the legal discovery process, including the identification, preservation, collection, review, and production of information relevant to litigation matters, regulatory inquiries, and internal investigations.
   

  

 Duties will include but will not be limited to: performing custodial/data source research and identification, along with the preservation, collection, disposition, and/or secure delivery of data within pre\-defined Service Level Agreements; acting as liaison between LDM and its partners, participating in end\-to\-end eDiscovery projects and programs with a focus on process improvement; managing various projects with multiple stakeholders; coordinating project milestones and deliverables; working directly with all staff levels from analysts to senior management, and delivering results on both near\- and long\-term initiatives.
   

  

**Job Responsibilities**
* Act as a point\-of\-contact for legal teams, advising and coordinating discovery activities.
* Respond to and fulfill eDiscovery requests across various data sources, including but not limited to electronic communications, voice, structured and unstructured data sources.
* Coordinate the discovery lifecycle among all collaborating parties, including the firm's internal attorneys, outside counsel, vendors, and the firm's internal discovery IT group.
* Conduct early matter outreach, discovery planning, budgeting, custodian scoping, tracking, status reporting, managing to timelines and overseeing production requests.
* Coordinate with internal IT and business partners, and external vendors in support of request fulfillment, including restoration of data with appropriate chain\-of\-custody documentation, where required.
* Oversee day\-to\-day case details for certain matter types. Maintain a level of understanding of the business uses for the systems from which data is being requested and proactively address questions related to fulfilling such requests.
* Act as a liaison between the eDiscovery team and global systems and data center contacts, including but not limited to tape operations areas/data centers and third parties, to manage various legal discovery requests.
* Facilitate the flow of documents and knowledge throughout the discovery process: direct documents into the appropriate workstreams and transmit questions, answers, and information to/from the managed review vendor and internal or external counsel.
* Support the continuous improvement of eDiscovery operational processes globally, including request processing, research, preservation, collection, disposition, delivery, and control.
* Draft and/or review process management documentation, maintain organized updates and detailed matter/project notes and documentation.
* Data\-driven problem solving and decision making; manage and appropriately escalate delivery impediments, risks, issues, and changes associated with process enhancement initiatives.


**Required Qualifications, Capabilities, And Skills**
* Law Graduate / J.D. from an accredited law school. Attorney must be licensed to practice law and a member in good standing in the state/jurisdiction in which the position is based or otherwise in compliance with the in\-house counsel registration rules of that state/jurisdiction.
* Minimum 5\+ years of discovery experience at a financial services provider, consulting firm, discovery vendor, or top\-tier law firm, with cross\-EDRM hands\-on and advisory experience.
* Understanding of firm change management processes and procedures (SDLC, etc.) and experience working in a secure environment with sensitive data, including PII.
* Familiarity with Electronically Stored Information ESI investigation procedures, preservation, disposition, recovery, and analysis of data from a variety of electronic communication, voice, and unstructured systems (e.g., M365 Purview, MS Exchange, Connected Archive, Lotus Notes, Robocopy, OnTrack, Hard Drives, Ascent, Digital Safe, NICE, Cisco, SharePoint), backup tape infrastructure (ArcServe, TSM, TDP, NetBackup), structured data systems, databases and/or EDRM (eDiscovery Reference Model), or litigation support\-related experience.
* Project Management, ITIL, ACEDS, PMP background.
* Familiarity with, knowledge of, or understanding of legal chain\-of\-custody requirements, regulatory processes, and basic Federal Rules of Civil Procedure.
* Self\-motivated, highly flexible, organized, and team\-oriented, with the ability to track multiple workstreams and manage confidential and/or sensitive, time\-critical, and competing priorities and projects. Comfortable responding to shifting priorities and working independently with minimal supervision.

title: Data Protection Officer
description:
**Primary Purpose** 




 To own, maintain and improve our data protection and privacy compliance framework, ensuring lawful, fair and transparent processing of personal data across our processing sites in the UK, EU, India, Philippines, US and Canada.
 



  





**Main Responsibilities:** 




 The Data Protection Officer is responsible for proactively managing and improving our data protection compliance framework, driving privacy accountability and lawful processing across the organisation, partnering with IT, Operations, Engineering, HR, Procurement and business stakeholders to embed practical data protection controls and support compliant growth.
 


* Own and maintain the data protection governance framework, including policies, standards, procedures and supporting documentation.
* Maintain and manage the Record of Processing Activities (ROPA), ensuring processing activities, data flows, systems, suppliers and international transfers are accurately documented and kept up to date.
* Lead and produce Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIAs), Legitimate Interest Assessments (LIAs), EU Standard Contract Clauses (SCC) and other privacy risk assessments for new and changed processing activities and transfers.
* Review, negotiate and advise on client and supplier data processing agreements (DPAs), privacy clauses and international data transfer provisions.
* Monitor compliance with applicable privacy and data protection legislation across our processing sites in the UK, EU, India, Philippines, US and Canada, escalating gaps and driving remediation actions.
* Provide practical guidance on lawful bases for processing, data subject rights, retention, minimisation, privacy by design and cross\-border transfers.
* Support the management of personal data breaches, including triage, risk assessment, notification decision\-making, client communications and post\-incident review.
* Work with supplier owners and procurement teams to assess third\-party privacy risk and ensure appropriate due diligence and contractual controls are in place.
* Develop and deliver data protection training and awareness to employees and support responses to client privacy questionnaires, audits and compliance requests.
* Define and report privacy KPIs, incidents, risks, audit findings and action plans to senior leadership, while working with IT, Operations, Engineering and wider business units to identify risks and scale good practice.



  





**Professional skills/ experience:** 



* 5\+ years in data protection, privacy compliance or information governance with hands\-on responsibility for operational privacy activities.
* Proven experience reviewing and negotiating client and supplier DPAs and advising on practical contractual privacy requirements.
* Strong experience producing DPIAs, maintaining ROPAs and supporting data subject rights, retention and international transfer compliance.
* Working knowledge of UK GDPR, EU GDPR and broader international privacy requirements across the UK, EU, India, Philippines, US and Canada.
* Professional certification such as CIPP/E, CIPM, EU GDPR Practitioner or equivalent privacy qualification desirable.
* Able to translate privacy risk into business impact and influence stakeholders at all levels.



  





**Personal Qualities** 



* Problem solver.
* Great with people, can build trust and rapport across the entire organisation.
* Good communicator with clients and internally.
* Team Player commitment and flexible.
* Ability to prioritise and quickly resolve issues.
* Attention to detail.

 This is an opportunity to join a business with broad international operations and take ownership of group insurance matters across a varied and fast\-moving risk landscape. You will work across insurance, trade, logistics, legal, finance, and commercial stakeholders, helping ensure the Group's coverage remains aligned to its activities while supporting effective claims handling, renewals, and contract review.
   

  

 As Senior Manager Group Insurance, you will oversee TORQ Group's insurance portfolio with particular responsibility for marine and cargo risks, complex claims, policy renewals, and insurance\-related contract review. The role is suited to someone who brings strong commercial judgement, a hands\-on approach, and the ability to operate confidently across jurisdictions and functions while helping strengthen insurance processes across the Group.
   

  

**Responsibilities**
* Manage and coordinate TORQ Group's insurance portfolio to ensure that business activities, assets, stock, liabilities, and people are appropriately insured
* Maintain complete and accurate records of policies, endorsements, certificates, coverage limits, deductibles, warranties, and renewal dates
* Monitor policy conditions, warranties, and notification requirements to protect the Group's ability to recover under its policies
* Coordinate premium payments, reconciliations, refunds, and policy adjustments with Finance and other relevant teams
* Provide insurance documents required by customers, suppliers, lenders, landlords, and other contractual counterparties
* Manage insurance requirements arising from the international and domestic movement, storage, and handling of commodities

* Identify insurable risks arising from new products, markets, geographies, contracts, logistics structures, and business activities
* Work with Legal, Trade Operations, and commercial teams on insurance and indemnity provisions in sales and purchase contracts, logistics, warehousing, freight, chartering, processing, and financing arrangements
* Flag adverse insurance provisions, uninsured exposures, and contractual obligations that require additional cover
* Recommend appropriate insurance solutions and practical risk\-mitigation measures
* Maintain effective working relationships with insurers, brokers, and specialist advisers
* Coordinate with surveyors, loss adjusters, investigators, marine consultants, claims advisers, and external lawyers
* Monitor service delivery, maintain momentum on open matters, and escalate performance or responsiveness concerns when required
* Provide accurate management information and strengthen insurance processes across the Group
* Maintain clear reporting on policies, premiums, notified and outstanding claims, settlements, recoveries, exposures, and renewals
* Analyse claims trends and recurring loss events, and recommend practical preventive measures

**Qualifications**
 MBA or equivalent postgraduate management qualification from a recognised institution, or an LLB or equivalent legal qualification from a recognised university or law school.
   

  

 ACII, Insurance Institute of India qualifications or an equivalent recognised insurance certification would be an advantage.
   

  

**Experience**
 Five to seven years of relevant post\-qualification experience, including at least five years gained after completion of the MBA or legal qualification.
   

  

 Relevant experience gained in one of the following backgrounds: a leading insurer, particularly in commercial, marine, liability or claims functions; a reputable insurance broker managing complex corporate accounts or claims; a commodity trading company, import\-export house, shipping or logistics business, or large corporate insurance function; or a reputable law firm with meaningful experience in insurance, marine matters, claims or insurance disputes.
   

  

**Knowledge and Technical Exposure**
 Marine and cargo insurance, international trade and shipping, Incoterms and cross\-border transactions.
   

  

 Commercial policy interpretation, claims documentation, surveys and loss adjustment, subrogation and recovery.
   

  

 Trade credit, liability, property and corporate insurance programmes.
   

  

 Commodity, import\-export, warehousing, logistics and supply\-chain risks.
   

  

**Core Competencies**
 Strong analytical ability and commercial judgement.
   

  

 Confidence in interpreting policy wording and contractual provisions.
   

  

 Excellent negotiation, written communication and stakeholder\-management skills with senior internal and external stakeholders.
   

  

 High attention to detail, disciplined documentation and the ability to manage competing deadlines.
   

  

 Eligibility to work in India.

**Job Description:**
**About the role:**
 Legal Counsel, India is the primary legal contact for Takeda’s businesses and legal entities in India. Reporting directly to the Lead Counsel, Asia Pacific (APAC), the role provides end\-to\-end, practical legal support across commercial, medical, regulatory, market access, manufacturing and supply, business development, finance, HR, procurement, digital and other business functions. The Legal Counsel also supports Takeda’s Innovation Capability Center (ICC) and the evolving Global Capability Model (GCM) in India.
   

  

 As a core member of the Country Leadership Team, the Legal Counsel brings sound legal judgment to business decisions, translates complex requirements into clear options and recommendations, and helps the organization move with appropriate speed while protecting patients, Takeda and its reputation.
   

  

 The role has particular responsibility for legal support connected with the launch and commercialization of Takeda’s vaccine portfolio in India. It also supports business development, strategic collaborations and other partnerships with third parties.
   

  

 The role will also serve as Whole\-time Company Secretary for the relevant Takeda entity or entities in India and will oversee corporate secretarial and governance compliance.
   

  

 The role combines independent ownership of complex matters with close collaboration across APAC and the wider Global Legal, Ethics \& Compliance organization.
   

  

**How you will contribute:**
* Serve as the primary legal advisor for Takeda’s businesses and legal entities in India, providing timely, practical and risk\-based advice across day\-to\-day operations and material business matters.
* Partner with the India Country Leadership Team and relevant APAC and global stakeholders, bringing an independent legal perspective and enabling informed, timely and accountable decision\-making.
* Lead and coordinate legal support for local manufacturing initiatives.
* Advise on business development and third\-party collaborations, including licensing, commercialization, distribution, services and other strategic arrangements.
* Draft, review and negotiate a broad range of agreements, including commercial, manufacturing and supply, distribution, licensing, services, procurement, HCP/HCO, medical, market access, patient\-support, digital, employment, finance and real\-estate agreements.
* Provide legal support to the India Innovation Capability Center and Takeda’s Global Capability Model
* Promote scalable and efficient legal support by developing fit\-for\-purpose templates, playbooks and self\-service guidance, and by directing lower\-risk work to the appropriate business or capability owner while retaining Legal involvement where it adds material value.
* Perform the duties of Whole\-time Company Secretary for the relevant Indian entity or entities, ensuring compliance with applicable corporate, secretarial and governance requirements.
* Coordinate corporate secretary work with global Corporate Governance team
* Identify, assess and manage legal and regulatory risks, monitor relevant legislative developments and ensure appropriate stakeholders understand and implement required actions.
* Advise on competition law, anti\-bribery and corruption, privacy and digital matters, employment, disputes, investigations, audits, product and promotional matters, intellectual property interfaces and interactions with regulators and industry associations, in coordination with relevant subject\-matter experts.
* Manage litigation, arbitration, mediation, pre\-dispute strategy and external legal matters to protect Takeda’s rights and support effective resolution.
* Select and manage external counsel and other legal providers with disciplined scoping, quality oversight and cost management, using external support where specialist expertise or capacity is genuinely required.
* Build legal capability across the organization through clear communication, practical training, coaching and guidance, and contribute to APAC and global Legal, Ethics \& Compliance initiatives and communities of practice.
* Continuously improve legal processes and ways of working by simplifying complexity, reducing duplication, leveraging data, digital tools and AI responsibly, and focusing resources on work with the greatest patient, business and risk impact.
* Model Takeda’s values and expected leadership behaviors by putting patients at the center, collaborating with respect, acting with integrity, constructively challenging when needed, taking accountability and delivering priorities with urgency and quality.


**Education and professional qualifications:**
* Law degree from a recognized law school and qualification to practice law in India, with current good standing where applicable.
* Current membership with the Institute of Company Secretaries of India (ICSI), and eligibility to be appointed as a Whole\-time Company Secretary, is required.


**Experience:**
* At least 8 years of relevant post\-qualification legal experience in a leading law firm and/or the legal department of a multinational organization, with maturity and independence expected for a senior role.
* Strong experience advising a complex business in India across commercial, corporate, regulatory and operational matters; pharmaceutical industry experience is strongly preferred.
* Demonstrated experience with corporate secretarial work, corporate governance, Companies Act requirements, Board processes.
* Experience supporting product launches and negotiating complex agreements.
* Experience supporting capability centers, shared\-services environments, global operating models or cross\-border transformation is an advantage.


**Capabilities:**
* Excellent legal analysis, drafting and negotiation skills, combined with strong commercial judgment and the ability to distinguish material risk from manageable operational issues.
* Able to operate independently, prioritize competing demands and deliver clear recommendations in a fast\-moving environment.
* Pragmatic, solutions\-focused and comfortable making decisions within clear accountability, while escalating material issues early.

title: Litigation Manager — Legal (Litigation & Dispute Resolution)
description:
**ABOUT THE ROLE** 




  





 You will own the company's litigation portfolio end to end — commercial disputes, arbitrations, recovery matters, contractual claims and regulatory proceedings. This is a coordination and outcome role: you will not typically appear in court yourself, but you will instruct and manage a panel of external advocates across multiple forums and cities, keep internal business teams aligned, and drive matters toward resolution rather than allowing them to drift. The company operates across multiple jurisdictions and forums, so comfort with running parallel matters at different stages is essential.
 



  





**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES** 




  





**External counsel management** 



* Act as the single point of contact for all external advocates, law firms and senior counsel across matters
* Brief counsel and review drafts — plaints, written statements, applications, affidavits, written submissions — before filing
* Track hearing calendars, ensure counsel readiness, and follow up on adjournments and non\-effective hearings
* Evaluate and onboard new counsel; maintain a panel with clearly defined scope and fee terms



  





**End\-to\-end matter tracking** 



* Maintain a live litigation tracker covering stage, next date, exposure, counsel and internal owner for every matter
* Prepare periodic status reports and dashboards for management and the board
* Flag limitation dates, statutory timelines (including Section 29A mandate periods in arbitrations) and filing deadlines proactively
* Drive matters to closure — identify stalled proceedings and escalate to expedite



  





**Internal stakeholder coordination** 



* Work with Finance, Projects, Sales, Procurement and Operations to gather documents, facts and witness inputs
* Translate legal positions into commercial language for business teams and management
* Support commercial teams on dispute avoidance — escalation notices, demand notices and pre\-litigation settlement discussions



  





**Commercial and cost control** 



* Review counsel fee proposals against agreed schedules; validate invoices before payment
* Track legal spend by matter and against budget
* Assess settlement options on a cost\-benefit basis and present recommendations



  





**Documentation and risk** 



* Maintain case files, pleadings, orders and evidence in an organised, retrievable system
* Support contract teams with lessons learned from disputes — recurring clause failures, warranty/DLP issues, payment defaults



  





**REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS** 




  




* LL.B. from a recognised university; enrolled with a Bar Council
* 4–5 years' experience in litigation — in a law firm/chambers with in\-house exposure, or within an in\-house legal team
* Demonstrated experience running multiple matters simultaneously across different forums
* Working knowledge of the Civil Procedure Code, Arbitration and Conciliation Act 1996, Commercial Courts Act 2015, and NCLT/IBC procedure
* Strong drafting review ability — able to spot gaps in a pleading even where counsel has drafted it
* Proven track record of coordinating with external counsel and non\-legal internal teams



  





**PREFERRED** 




  




* Exposure to construction, real estate, infrastructure or manufacturing disputes
* Experience with arbitration proceedings (institutional and ad\-hoc), including Sections 9, 11, 17, 29A and 34 applications
* Familiarity with legal\-tech or matter\-management systems, or having built a litigation tracker from scratch
* Experience negotiating counsel fee structures and managing legal budgets
* Multi\-state litigation exposure (Maharashtra, Karnataka, Delhi)



  





**WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR** 




  




* Ownership — treats every matter as theirs to close, not merely to report on
* Follow\-through — persistent with counsel and internal teams; things do not slip
* Commercial judgment — knows when to fight and when to settle
* Clarity — can explain a complex dispute to a non\-lawyer director in five minutes
* Composure under deadline — same\-day filings and urgent applications are part of the job

title: RMC Governance Lead - Vice President
description:
**Job Description**
 Bring your expertise to JPMorgan Chase. As part of Risk Management and Compliance, you are at the center of keeping JPMorgan Chase strong and resilient. You help the firm grow its business in a responsible way by anticipating new and emerging risks, and using your expert judgement to solve real\-world challenges that impact our company, customers and communities. Our culture in Risk Management and Compliance is all about thinking outside the box, challenging the status quo and striving to be best\-in\-class.
   

  

 As a Vice President in the Credit Risk Governance team, you will collaborate with global Wealth Management functions, including Risk, Lending Solutions, Operations, Legal, and Compliance. Your role will involve working with the Wealth Management Risk function to develop and maintain policies, standards, guidelines, and procedures, including regulatory compliance measures. You will work closely with the Front Office to assess business needs and develop risk controls to achieve revenue targets and business growth. Your responsibilities will also include maintaining a full inventory of documents and ensuring they are clear, concise, and user\-friendly. You will assist in developing and implementing the business risk management framework, including risk governance and controls, organization structure, policies and procedures, and risk measures and metrics. You will also be responsible for delivering large\-scale risk and regulatory change and technical initiatives. Communication of changes, detailing requirements, and strategic risk management objectives to large working groups, including senior management, will be a key part of your role. You will also work with internal groups such as Credit, Investment, and Fiduciary Risk areas, as well as Compliance, Legal, and Operations on matters related to risk controls, model\-assessments, incidents, and infrastructure projects. Lastly, you will provide support and guidance for audits and regulatory examinations.
   

  

**Job Responsibilities**
* Work with Wealth Management Risk function to develop and maintain policies, standards, guidelines, and procedures, including regulatory compliance measures and risk advisory within the Risk Management Program.
* Work closely with the Front Office to assess business needs and further develop risk controls to efficiently achieve revenue target and new business growth.
* Play a key role in the hierarchy and design of documentation by maintaining full inventory of documents.
* Review documentation to ensure it is clear, concise, and user\-friendly. Perform ongoing updates to existing documentation to ensure they remain accurate and relevant.
* Assist in developing, design, implementation, and support of line of business risk management framework, including but not limited to: Risk governance and controls, organization structure, policies and procedures, three lines of defense, risk measures and metrics (risk appetite and limits, monitoring and escalation).
* Deliver large\-scale risk and regulatory change and technical initiatives.
* Communicate changes including detailing requirements and strategic risk management objectives/updates to large working groups, including senior management.
* Work alongside internal groups such as Credit, Investment, and Fiduciary Risk areas as well as Compliance, Legal, and Operations on matters related to risk controls, model\-assessments, incidents, and infrastructure projects.
* Provide support and guidance for audits and regulatory examinations.


**Required Qualifications, Capabilities, And Skills**
* Bachelor's Degree or commensurate related job experience
* 5\+ years of experience in Auditing, Accounting, Internal Control and/or Credit Analysis with focus on Wholesale Credit Risk
* Strong business writing skills
* Experience in Wholesale Audit, Compliance, Operational, and/or Regulatory Risk Management
* Demonstrated ability to collaborate cross\-functions to achieve measurable results
* Strong organizational skills
* Ability to manage and prioritize multiple requests at the same time
* Detail oriented with strong analytical skills
* Proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint


**Preferred Qualifications, Capabilities, And Skills**
* Project and/or Change Management experience preferred


**ABOUT US**
 JPMorganChase, one of the oldest financial institutions, offers innovative financial solutions to millions of consumers, small businesses and many of the world's most prominent corporate, institutional and government clients under the J.P. Morgan and Chase brands. Our history spans over 200 years and today we are a leader in investment banking, consumer and small business banking, commercial banking, financial transaction processing and asset management.
   

  

 We recognize that our people are our strength and the diverse talents they bring to our global workforce are directly linked to our success. We are an equal opportunity employer and place a high value on diversity and inclusion at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of any protected attribute, including race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, marital or veteran status, pregnancy or disability, or any other basis protected under applicable law. We also make reasonable accommodations for applicants' and employees' religious practices and beliefs, as well as mental health or physical disability needs. Visit our FAQs for more information about requesting an accommodation.
   

  

**About The Team**
 J.P. Morgan Asset \& Wealth Management delivers industry\-leading investment management and private banking solutions. Asset Management provides individuals, advisors and institutions with strategies and expertise that span the full spectrum of asset classes through our global network of investment professionals. Wealth Management helps individuals, families and foundations take a more intentional approach to their wealth or finances to better define, focus and realize their goals.
   

  

 Risk Management helps the firm understand, manage and anticipate risks in a constantly changing environment. The work covers areas such as evaluating country\-specific risk, understanding regulatory changes and determining credit worthiness. Risk Management provides independent oversight and maintains an effective control environment.

title: Regional Employee Relations Lead - APAC
description:

 Hybrid, permanent, full\-time

 Global Head of Employee Relations
   

  

**About The Role**
 We are looking for a
 **Regional Employee Relations Lead – Asia Pacific** 
 to lead BSI’s Employee Relations activity across a diverse and complex regional portfolio.
   

  

 Supporting BSI businesses across markets including China, India, Japan, Malaysia, Vietnam, Indonesia, Korea and Australia, you will provide regional leadership on complex employee relations matters while helping embed a consistent, high\-quality approach to case management, governance and employee experience.
   

  

 This is both a strategic and operational leadership role. You will oversee complex and high\-risk ER activity, advise on organisational change and restructuring, strengthen regional capability and ensure evolving employment legislation is translated into practical guidance for leaders and People teams.
   

  

 You will also lead in\-country ER Specialists across
 **China, India and Japan** 
 , while working closely with HR Generalists and Regional HR Managers across the wider APAC region.
   

  

**Key Responsibilities**
* Lead and oversee employee relations activity across the Asia Pacific region, ensuring complex and high\-risk cases are managed effectively and consistently.

* Demonstrable experience managing complex and high\-risk employee relations matters, including within jurisdictions such as Japan and Korea.
* Experience advising on organisational change, restructuring and other complex workforce matters.
* Strong understanding of employee representation models across APAC, including unions, employee forums and collective arrangements.
* Experience creating or strengthening ER policies, frameworks, processes and ways of working.

**Do you believe the world deserves excellence?**

title: Senior Compliance Analyst
description:
**Role in a Nutshell** 




 BrowserStack's Compliance team owns the company's compliance posture across the security
 



 and privacy frameworks it operates under globally, making that posture verifiable to customers,
 



 auditors, and regulators.
 



 As a Compliance Analyst, you will work across certification audits, framework implementation,
 



 customer security assurance, contract review, and compliance operations. Depending on your
 



 experience, you may support or independently own different parts of these processes.
 



 We are looking for someone who is self\-motivated, takes ownership of problems rather than just
 



 tasks, and enjoys turning ambiguous requirements into practical processes. This role offers the
 



 opportunity to build deep expertise in compliance while gradually taking ownership of larger
 



 areas of the function.
 



  





 This role requires you to work remotely, based out of Mumbai. Relocation to Mumbai is mandatory.
 



  





 The level of ownership will vary based on your experience, with opportunities to progressively
 



 take ownership of larger areas of the compliance program.
 



**Responsibilities** 




 ● Support and, based on experience, independently manage BrowserStack's compliance certifications and audit cycles, including audit planning, evidence collection, control testing, documentation, remediation, and auditor coordination.
 



 ● Implement and maintain controls for frameworks such as SOC 2, ISO 27001, ISO 27701, ISO 42001, and applicable data privacy regulations, working closely with control owners across the organization.
 



 ● Track audit, framework, and remediation action items through closure and maintain an accurate and up\-to\-date view of BrowserStack's control environment.
 



 ● Translate framework and regulatory requirements into practical, workable controls in collaboration with Engineering, Product, IT, Legal, and other teams.
 



 ● Respond to customer security questionnaires, RFIs, and security assurance requests, including handling more complex or technical questions as experience grows.
 



 ● Maintain and improve the internal knowledge base used to support customer security responses, ensuring information remains accurate as the product, controls, and certifications evolve.
 



 ● Contribute to BrowserStack's public\-facing security documentation and Trust Center, ensuring that published information accurately reflects the company's actual control environment.
 



 ● Review vendor and customer contracts for security, privacy, and compliance risks against established review standards and support the development of reusable review guidelines and clause libraries.
 



 ● Partner with Engineering, Product, and Customer\-facing teams to understand
 



 technical or product\-specific compliance requirements and translate them into clear, reusable responses.
 



 ● Read and evaluate security documentation, audit reports, architecture diagrams, and related evidence to determine whether they adequately support compliance
 



 requirements or customer\-facing claims.
 



 ● Identify recurring gaps, manual processes, or inefficiencies across compliance operations and propose practical improvements to processes, documentation, or tooling.
 



 ● Work with tools such as Jira and Confluence to manage compliance workflows, documentation, and action items.
 



 ● Contribute to the evaluation and adoption of GRC, continuous compliance, Trust Center, questionnaire management, and contract review tools.
 



  





**Requirements** 




 ● 1–5 years of experience in compliance, GRC, security assurance, IT audit, information security, or a related field, ideally in a B2B SaaS or technology environment.
 



 ● Working knowledge of security and privacy frameworks and regulations such as SOC 2, ISO 27001, ISO 27701, ISO 42001, GDPR, or equivalent, with the ability to interpret and apply these requirements to practical compliance activities.
 



 ● Hands\-on experience with, or exposure to, audit and compliance activities such as audit planning, evidence collection, control testing, control implementation, documentation, remediation, or auditor coordination.
 



 ● Ability to translate framework and regulatory requirements into practical, workable controls and collaborate with teams across Engineering, Product, IT, Legal, and other functions to implement them.
 



 ● Ability to read and interpret security documentation, audit reports, architecture diagrams, cloud configurations, and other technical information well enough to assess whether evidence adequately supports a compliance requirement.
 



 ● Experience responding to or supporting customer security questionnaires, RFIs, and security assurance requests, with the ability to communicate technical and compliance information clearly to non\-technical audiences.
 



 ● Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate technical,
 



 security, privacy, and legal concepts into clear, customer\-ready and auditor\-ready language.
 



 ● Strong ownership and problem\-solving mindset, with the ability to identify gaps,
 



 investigate root causes, and drive issues through to resolution rather than simply
 



 completing assigned tasks.
 



 ● Ability to manage multiple compliance activities, maintain accurate documentation, and track audit, framework, and remediation action items through closure.
 



 ● Comfortable working with collaborative tools such as Jira and Confluence for documentation, workflow management, and compliance tracking.
 



 ● Exposure to or experience with GRC and continuous compliance platforms, Trust Center or security questionnaire tooling, or contract review tooling is a plus.
 



 ● Exposure to vendor and customer contract reviews from a security, privacy, or compliance perspective is a plus.
 



 ● Experience working directly with auditors, control owners, Engineering, Product, or Customer\-facing teams to resolve compliance requirements is a plus.
 



 ● Professional certifications such as CISA, CISM, CRISC, ISO 27001 Lead Auditor/Lead Implementer, or CIPP/E are a plus.
 



  





**What You'll Get to Work On** 




  





 This role provides exposure across the broader compliance function, including:
 



 ● Security and privacy compliance frameworks
 



 ● Certification and audit programs
 



 ● Control design and implementation
 



 ● Customer security assurance
 



 ● Security questionnaires and RFIs
 



 ● Contract and compliance reviews
 



 ● Trust Center and security documentation
 



 ● Compliance processes, automation, and tooling

title: Head of Legal
description:
**Head of Legal** 




  





 Legal here is a profit function, not a review desk — and you're the one who prices it that way. The paper prices value, wins faster, and protects the assets that compound: outcome contracts, partner paper, marketplace terms, IP architecture, and your own Locked numbers.
 



  





**What are we looking for** 




  





**Solver? Absolutely. But not the usual kind.** 
 Contracting, done right, isn't a defense function — it's how value gets priced, protected, and compounded. If you read a deal the way an architect reads a structure — where the risk sits, where the margin sits, and how to build paper that holds under both negotiation and audit — we want to connect.
 



  




* Principal, not custodian.
* Reads risk the way an engineer reads load\-bearing steel.
* Builds the paper once, so it holds — not the paper you redraft every time someone pushes back.
* Comfortable being the last signature before something becomes real.
* Thinks in systems: this clause, this precedent, this margin, for years — not just this deal.



  





**This Isn’t for Everyone.** 
 But if you’ve ever redlined a contract and thought about the deal it
 *should* 
 have been — not just the risk it should have avoided — we’d love to chat with you.
 



  





**Your Mission: The Role** 




*solving for better.* 




  





 This firm sells outcome contracts — fixed, at\-risk, and gainshare against verified numbers. It admits partners on profit points, lists products on CSP marketplaces, and deploys engineers into partner programs on tour terms. Every one of those is a contracting innovation, and each one either generates margin or blocks it. The paper is the pricing instrument. You own the paper.
 



 You build the function from an empty seat: three people, live in six months, chartered like every other squad here — a Locked number, an eval discipline, agents as the workforce, humans on judgment. If your instinct is to steer an outcome fee back to time\-and\-materials, or to say no before you've priced the yes, this isn't your seat.
 



 If you read a P\&L as fluently as a clause, treat a term sheet as a pricing instrument, and don't lose energy in a hostile counterparty round — this is your seat at the table.
 



  





**Your Responsibilities** 




*what you will wake up to solve.* 




  





**Price the Value** 



* **Own the Outcome Paper:** 
 Structure fixed, at\-risk, and gainshare contracts against verified numbers — every clause a pricing instrument, not boilerplate. Gainshare converts delivery excellence into revenue that hourly paper never captures.
* **Clear the Marketplace:** 
 Get listing terms cleared on both CSP marketplaces so commit\-burn purchasing becomes procurement\-free revenue. Paper that isn't cleared is revenue that doesn't exist.
* **Write the Moat's Legal Layer:** 
 Partnership deeds, vesting, and clawback mechanics validated across India, the US, the UK, and Singapore; an IP and two\-brand trademark architecture that protects the patterns and agents that compound.
* **Cut the Cycle:** 
 Every day removed from paper cycles is pipeline conversion. NDA turnaround under 24 hours; MSA and SOW under 5 days — by month 6\.



**Build the Agentic Function** 



* **Agents Draft First, Always:** 
 Stand up drafting agents grounded in a versioned clause library so no contract starts from a blank page; humans redline and decide. 80% of routine paper agent\-first\-drafted by month 6\.
* **Playbooks as Code:** 
 Codify negotiation positions, fallback ladders, and escalation thresholds per contract type. Review agents enforce them; only deviations reach a human.
* **Run the Eval Harness:** 
 A gold\-standard contract set with known issues; every agent measured on catch rate and false\-positive rate per clause type before deployment and on every model refresh. Legal is not exempt from evaluation.
* **Hire Above Your Own Bar:** 
 Hire the talent required to achieve the function's objectives — a three\-person team, not a growing headcount. Make self\-serve standard paper cover 50% of requests so hiring above the bar, not adding more of it, is how you scale.



**Hold the Judgment Line** 



* **Human\-Only Gates, Non\-Negotiable:** 
 Signatures, novel structures, regulatory filings, disputes, and anything touching the verification instrument or partner admission stay with you. Zero agent\-drafted paper is signed without human review.
* **Zero Ambiguity Restatements:** 
 No verified\-number restatement is ever traceable to contract ambiguity. The paper is precise enough that the number holds.
* **Buy Depth, Don't Hire It:** 
 Run outside counsel across the US, UK, Singapore, and the Middle East as an elastic layer, bought per matter and managed against a spend\-per\-matter number — down 40% against the month\-1 baseline.



**Report a Number, Not a Cost Line** 



* **Legal's Own Ledger:** 
 Report a revenue\-enabled number to the Betting Table — contract\-cycle days removed from pursuits, gainshare clauses executed, marketplace revenue unlocked — not only a spend line.
* **Own Every Locked Number:** 
 You are accountable for each target above and for the human\-only gates. Not the team. You.



  





**The DNA of a ‘Searcian’** 




*superpowers we value.* 




  





**The ‘happier’ core** 



* **happier\-at\-heart:** 
**h** 
 umble,
 **a** 
 daptable,
 **p** 
 ositive,
 **p** 
 assionate,
 **i** 
 nnovative,
 **e** 
 xcellence\-minded,
 **r** 
 esponsible.
* **happier\-in\-action:** 
 Not just a poster on the wall; It's how we make decisions, treat each other, show up for clients \& hire or promote people.
* **Thinks like a founder. Acts like an owner.**
* **Always in Beta:** 
 Relentless curiosity. Openness to learn, un\-learn, and re\-learn.
* **Real Optimist:** 
 Views all setbacks as opportunities.
* **Believes in truth over comfort. Ideas over titles. Learning over knowing.**
* **Embraces chaos with calm. Evolves faster than the market.**



  





**The ‘evlos’ mindset** 




 This is the "how" behind your work. It’s a deep\-seated drive to improve, discover, and own.
 


* **Solver\-core:** 
 Problem\-solving is not just a default setting for a Searcian, it is our genuine passion and makes ‘our eyes light up’. We actually solve problems to unwind \& relax.
* **Real improver:** 
 Searcians are built to push for better, not just settle for done. Real solvers Iterate to become better everyday and remain self\-driven.
* **Under\-promise \& over\-deliver.** 
 We love to create pleasant surprises.
* **Authentically original thinking:** 
 Asks the "why" that unlocks what's next. Brings unique, valuable perspectives to every discussion.
* **Built\-to\-last \+ engineered\-to\-scale:** 
 We don't lead with tools. We lead with foundations.
 **Process\-first, AI\-second.**
* **Super\-Learner:** 
 Learns faster, adapts smarter, levels up relentlessly. What you can do tomorrow matters more to us than what you did yesterday. Your learning curve beats experience.



  





**Functional Skills** 



* **P\&L Fluency:** 
 Reads a P\&L and models gainshare economics live — treats a contract as a pricing instrument, not a risk register.
* **Deal\-Room Presence:** 
 Holds the room with Partners, CSP sellers, and clients through a collapsed structure or a hostile round. Energy is a working tool here, not a personality note.
* **Principal's Judgment:** 
 Thinks like an owner of the business, not a service provider to it — knows which risks are worth carrying for margin.
* **Buy vs. Build Judgment:** 
 Knows when jurisdictional depth is worth buying per matter versus building in\-house — a capital\-allocation call, not a staffing default.
* **Function\-Builder Instinct:** 
 Designs a legal function as a system — clause library, playbooks, agents, people — not as a headcount request.



  





**Tech Superpowers** 



* **AI\-Native Legal Practice:** 
 Uses LLMs in your own legal workflow today — drafting, review, research — with an explicit quality\-control method, not just a prompt habit.
* **Agentic Legal Stack Literacy:** 
 Understands drafting agents, review agents, versioned clause libraries, and eval harnesses well enough to specify what the Legal Engineer builds and judge whether it's working.
* **CLM \& CRM Systems Fluency:** 
 Has run contract lifecycle on enterprise CLM tooling (Ironclad, Sirion, Icertis, Agiloft, or equivalent) integrated with a CRM — knows what routing, attribution, and audit trail look like in software.
* **Eval\-Minded:** 
 Treats catch rate and false\-positive rate as the language for whether legal automation is trustworthy. Evaluation, not vibes.



  





**Experience \& Relevance** 



* **12\+ years** 
 , India\-qualified, with personal ownership of US or UK enterprise commercial paper.
* **Outside\-Counsel Command:** 
 Has run outside counsel across three or more jurisdictions.
* **Business\-First Record:** 
 Has structured outcome\-based, gainshare, or at\-risk commercial paper — not just reviewed it. A business background or business\-family exposure is preferred.
* **Location:** 
 Pune, Mumbai, or Ahmedabad.



  





**Bonus Points (you will thrive if you have)** 



* **The "Founder" Bias:** 
 You've built a function, team, or practice from zero — not inherited one already running.
* **Cross\-Domain Judgment:** 
 You've applied your expertise somewhere outside your formal training — a deal, a structure, a risk call outside the textbook.
* **Startup Grit:** 
 You've worn multiple hats in a resource\-constrained environment and solved "0→1" problems.
* **Public Voice:** 
 You've written, spoken, or taught publicly in your domain — not just practiced it privately.

 is Bain’s client selection and acceptance process. Developed in partnership with our Industry and Capability Practice Areas, it helps ensure we can be proud of the work we take on.  The focus is nearly always on identifying the right mitigating actions to enable us to Proceed with Pride, although in some instances we will jointly decide not to proceed.

**Key tasks**






**1\. APAC  Client Selection and Acceptance Process – Lead and manage end\-to\-end risk assessments**

**4\. Resolution Execution Support** 



* Work closely with the Asset Resolution team in implementing approved resolution strategies.
* Support restructuring, enforcement, settlement and asset monetisation initiatives.
* Monitor resolution milestones, recovery actions and execution timelines.

**5\. Cross\-Functional Stakeholder Management** 



* Coordinate with internal teams and external legal, valuation, diligence and advisory professionals.

* Identify execution issues and coordinate their resolution.

 .

 .

title: Associate Director - Legal
description:
**About**
****About Us****
****Build the future of banking.****
 Zeta is a next\-generation banking technology company providing cloud\-native, fully stackable processing and core banking platforms for issuers. With a focus on scalability, compliance, and innovation, Zeta empowers financial institutions to modernize their technology infrastructure and deliver secure, seamless digital banking experiences.
 ****Our Impact and Growth****
 Our impact runs at real\-world scale. Today,
 **over 25 million cards are live on Zeta\-powered platforms across 7 countries, supported by a passionate team of 1,700\+ Zetanauts** 
 across India, the US, EMEA, and Asia. Backed by
 **SoftBank Vision Fund, Mastercard** 
 , and other reputed strategic investors, we reached a valuation of
 **$2 billion** 
 in Jan 1, 2025 .
 ****Our Product Lines****
 Our focus is on establishing product lines that focus on key outcomes by addressing real customer pain points, modernizing legacy systems, and strengthening core fundamentals. As a result, our systems and platforms support a wide range of banking and payments capabilities, including:
   

  

* Tachyon, our cloud\-native banking stack built for population\-scale systems
* Cipher, our unified authentication platform for secure, high\-volume banking environments
* Digital Credit as a Service, enabling banks to launch credit lines on UPI
* Elena, our intelligent and conversational AI platform for banking
* Pixel, India’s first digital\-native credit card, launched in partnership with HDFC Bank, for whom we also revamped their PayZapp mobile app: Winner of the Celent Model Bank Award for Payments Innovation 2024
* Sparrow, the leading card experience for non\-prime cardholders in the US


 …and more across cards, payments, lending, and core banking.
   

  

**Our Culture and Values**
 We are an engineering\-first organization that values ownership, bias for action, and long\-term thinking. Together, we solve some of the hardest problems in banking tech. Our culture is built around trust, collaboration, and creating the conditions for you to drive impact proportionate to your potential. Reinforcing our commitment to creating an inclusive and supportive workplace, we have been consistently recognized as a
 **Great Place to Work** 
 .
   

  

**If you want to build cutting\-edge banking tech that enables banks to serve millions reliably, securely, and at a population scale, Zeta is your playground.**
 Learn More About Zeta
   

  

 If you would like to learn more about how we have grown and evolved over the years,
 **watch our journey here** 
 . You can also explore
 **our website** 
 and follow us on
 **LinkedIn** 
**,** 
**Instagram,** 
**YouTube** 
**, and** 
**X** 
**.**
**About The Role**
 Zeta is seeking a Associate Director – Legal to serve as a strategic advisor within its legal team, supporting the company’s banking, payments, and technology business as it scales across India, the US, the UK, and other global markets.
   

  

 This is a high\-impact, product\-facing role for a seasoned banking and finance lawyer who can operate at the intersection of financial services regulation and cutting\-edge technology, ensuring Zeta’s products, partnerships, and client programs are designed and delivered in a manner that is legally sound and regulator\-ready. Reporting into Zeta’s India legal leadership and partnering closely with Product, Compliance, and Risk teams, the role carries significant autonomy and visibility — requiring an individual who can independently own matters end to end, negotiate directly with banks, NBFCs, and technology partners, run and manage a team of capable lawyers, and help shape the legal function of a fast\-growing, high\-growth fintech at the core of India’s digital banking transformation.
   

  

**Responsibilities**
**Product and platform legal support**
* Deliver day\-to\-day legal counsel across Zeta’s banking technology stack, covering card issuance, transaction processing, lending and loan management, core account and ledger functionality, and Digital Credit\-as\-a\-Service and Credit Line on UPI (CLOU), BNPL, and EMI\-conversion products.
* Advise product and engineering teams on the regulatory implications of platform features, including card management, real\-time authorization and settlement, digital lending, account lifecycle management, instrument lifecycle management (physical and virtual cards, tokens, and QR), transaction switching, and fraud and dispute management.


**Contract drafting, review, and negotiation**
* Draft, review, and negotiate agreements with banks, financial institutions, card networks, and technology partners, including platform licensing, SaaS and managed\-services arrangements, program\-management agreements, and BIN or balance\-sheet sponsorship deals underpinning Banking\-as\-a\-Service and embedded banking offerings.
* Structure co\-brand, affinity, and fintech partnership arrangements, and draft and negotiate credit card, debit card, prepaid instrument, and co\-branded card program agreements spanning retail, commercial, private\-label, and secured card products.
* Structure and paper credit lines, BNPL, and loan\-installment features and related payment and settlement arrangements, and negotiate digital lending, co\-lending, and lending service provider (LSP) agreements.
* Draft, negotiate, and manage fintech partnership, third\-party vendor, and platform licensing agreements, allocating responsibility, liability, and data\-handling obligations across Zeta, its clients, and its partners.


**Regulatory advisory**
* Advise on RBI guidelines including the Digital Lending Directions, Credit Card and Debit Card Issuance and Conduct Directions, and Master Direction on Outsourcing of IT Services; NPCI regulations governing UPI and RuPay; and PPI rules under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act — tracking evolving developments and assessing their impact on Zeta’s products and programs.
* Advise on card\-network rules, grievance redressal frameworks, and partner bank agreement requirements for card and payments programs.
* Advise on data privacy, cybersecurity, and data\-localization requirements under the DPDP Act and IT Act, and on legal considerations relevant to maintaining SOC 2, ISO 27001, and PCI DSS certifications.
* Provide legal input on regulatory filings, regulator queries and inspections, and legal risk assessments for new products and partnerships, and support the development of internal legal playbooks and templates.


**Broader legal support**
* While anchored in banking and finance law, comfortable providing practical legal support across other areas as they arise for a fast\-growing technology business, including corporate, commercial, employment, and technology or intellectual property matters.


**Skills**
* Regulatory and commercial acumen: Commercially minded, pragmatic; translates complex regulation into clear, actionable guidance for non\-legal stakeholders.
* Stakeholder management and communication: Strong communication and negotiation skills, sound and independent judgment, ability to counsel senior management strategically.
* Execution and prioritization: Highly organized and detail\-oriented; manages multiple matters simultaneously in a fast\-paced, high\-growth setting; ability to leverage AI for legal work highly preferred.
* Team leadership and people management: Ability to lead and manage a team effectively.
* Ownership and adaptability: Proactive self\-starter, energized by ambiguity, comfortable in unfamiliar areas of law, takes ownership of outcomes, thrives in a collaborative, product\-driven culture at the frontier of banking and fintech.


**Experience And Qualification**
* LLB or equivalent law degree from a recognized institution; qualified to practice law in India. LLM is a plus.
* 9–12 years of post\-qualification experience as a banking and finance lawyer, gained in a top tier law firm.
* H ands\-on expertise across digital lending, credit and debit cards, prepaid and co\-branded card programs, payments, and fintech regulation.
* Contract drafting \& negotiation: Strong contract drafting, review, and negotiation skills across commercial, technology, and financial\-services agreements.
